records.evidence_job: Practice breaking down one coherent free-response-style physics situation; interpret the shared representation, use an earlier conclusion in a later part, and make or justify a model/plan choice.
records.student_action: Interpret the shared stimulus, carry evidence forward between connected parts, and justify a physics plan/model choice.
records.student_text:
The supplied diagram is intended to represent a cart moving to the right at constant speed, but the force model is flawed. Use the same diagram for all parts.
(a) Identify the feature of the force diagram that conflicts with constant-speed straight-line motion.
(b) Based on the unequal horizontal arrows, what direction of net force does the flawed diagram imply?
(c) Describe how you would revise the horizontal force arrows so the model matches constant-speed motion.
(d) Explain how your revised net force predicts the cart’s motion and why that prediction is consistent with Newton’s First Law.
records.student_html:
The supplied diagram is intended to represent a cart moving to the right at constant speed, but the force model is flawed. Use the same diagram for all parts.

(a) Identify the feature of the force diagram that conflicts with constant-speed straight-line motion.

(b) Based on the unequal horizontal arrows, what direction of net force does the flawed diagram imply?

(c) Describe how you would revise the horizontal force arrows so the model matches constant-speed motion.

(d) Explain how your revised net force predicts the cart’s motion and why that prediction is consistent with Newton’s First Law.
records.answer: (a) the horizontal forces are unequal; (b) toward the longer horizontal arrow; (c) make opposing horizontal forces equal in magnitude; (d) net force becomes zero, so velocity remains constant.
records.answer_text: (a) the horizontal forces are unequal; (b) toward the longer horizontal arrow; (c) make opposing horizontal forces equal in magnitude; (d) net force becomes zero, so velocity remains constant.
records.solution_text: A constant-speed cart traveling in a straight line has zero net force. Unequal opposing arrows imply a nonzero resultant and therefore changing motion. The corrected model uses equal opposing horizontal forces; then Newton’s First Law supports unchanged velocity.
records.solution_html: A constant-speed cart traveling in a straight line has zero net force. Unequal opposing arrows imply a nonzero resultant and therefore changing motion. The corrected model uses equal opposing horizontal forces; then Newton’s First Law supports unchanged velocity.
